S6.01.note: The per-token naming is inner code; only the Theme switch is a visible control.
steps: Click Account menu at the bottom of the sidebar, then Settings.
Click Appearance in the Settings list, then Light under Theme.
Look at the page background, sidebar and panels.
Click Dark under Theme and compare the backgrounds again with Expected.
S6.01.where: Settings > Appearance > Theme (effect seen on page and panel backgrounds)

S6.02.note: Surface token names are inner; the visible check is the contrast between menu/dialog and page.
steps: Click the Account menu button at the bottom of the sidebar.
Compare the menu panel with the page behind it.
Click Settings to open the Settings dialog and compare its surface with the page.
Switch Theme between Light and Dark and check the raised surfaces still stand out from the page.
S6.02.where: Account menu > Settings (raised surface is seen on the account menu and dialogs)

S6.03.note: Text tokens are defined in CSS; I did not open a specific screen that shows only muted text.
steps: Open the sidebar and read the conversation titles.
Compare primary text with muted text such as hints in Settings > Appearance.
Switch Theme between Light and Dark and check both stay readable.
S6.03.where: Effect seen on any text, for example the sidebar conversation titles and the chat replies

S6.04.note: Subtle and strong rule tokens are inner CSS names; the check is visual.
steps: Click Settings from the Account menu, then Appearance.
Look at the borders around the Theme buttons.
Switch between Light and Dark and compare the border strength.
Compare with the border on the selected Theme button.
S6.04.where: Settings > Appearance (borders around the Theme buttons and the Motion buttons)

S6.05.note: Contrast on each accent is not verified by this step; only the visible change is.
steps: Click Account menu, then Settings, then Appearance.
Click each colour swatch under Accent colour.
Check the selected swatch shows a ring and a check mark.
Look at buttons and selected controls: their fill changes with the accent, and text on them stays readable.

S6.06.note: I did not locate one specific screen that shows all four status colours.
steps: Trigger a status message in the app, for example a failed or completed action.
Read its text and compare the contrast with the background in Light and in Dark theme.
S6.06.where: Effect seen on success, warning, error and info messages in the app

S6.07.note: Only message text changes font; the sans UI font is not switchable by this control.
steps: Click Account menu, then Settings, then Appearance.
Choose Serif under Chat font (options are Default, Sans, Serif, Dyslexic friendly).
Send a message and read the reply text.
Compare the reply text with the font before the change, and check code in the reply stays monospace.

S6.08.note: The Appearance page h1 is hidden on wide screens (md:hidden), so the title may be seen only at phone width.
steps: Open Settings, then Appearance.
Compare the size and weight of the page title and section titles.
Open another Settings section and check its headings use the same sizes.
S6.08.where: Headings on the Settings and chat pages (effect seen on the Appearance page title and section titles)

S6.09.note: Whether the OS large-text setting is also respected is not verified here.
steps: Click Account menu, then Settings, then Appearance.
Choose Large under Chat text size.
Open or send a chat and read a reply.
Choose Small, read the reply again, and compare the size with Default and Large.

S6.10.note: The 12px floor and AA contrast are inner rules; the visible check is the hint text.
steps: Open Settings, then Appearance.
Read the hint text under Contrast, for example System follows your device setting.
Compare the hint text size and contrast with the row labels above it.
S6.10.where: Settings > Appearance (small hint text under rows such as Contrast and Motion)

S6.11.note: The monospace family and size are inner CSS values; the visible check is code against body text.
steps: Click Account menu, then Settings, then Appearance.
Look at Code theme and pick a different theme if you want to compare.
Ask the chat for a short code snippet and read the code block.
Compare the code font with the reply text font, and change Chat font to Serif to check code stays monospace.
S6.11.where: Settings > Appearance > Code theme (code is shown in a chat reply)

S6.12.note: Line-height rules are inner CSS; the check is visual.
steps: Ask the chat for a reply with a heading and three or four lines of text.
Compare the spacing between the lines of one paragraph.
Compare the line spacing of the heading with the text under it.
S6.12.where: Effect seen in multi-line chat replies and headings

S6.13.note: The paragraph gap rule is inner CSS.
steps: Ask the chat for an answer with three separate paragraphs.
Measure the gap between paragraphs and compare the gaps.
S6.13.where: Effect seen in chat replies with several paragraphs

S6.14.note: List indentation is an inner CSS rule.
steps: Ask the chat for a list with nested sub-items.
Compare the indent of the first level with the indent of the nested level.
S6.14.where: Effect seen in chat replies with bulleted or numbered lists

S6.15.note: The padding value is inner CSS; the visible check is the space around code text.
steps: Ask the chat for a code snippet and look at the space inside the code block edges.
Open Settings, then Appearance, and turn Wrap long code lines on.
Ask for a code line that is long and compare how it wraps inside the block padding.
S6.15.where: Effect seen inside code blocks in chat replies, and Settings > Appearance > Wrap long code lines

S6.16.note: Table padding is an inner CSS rule; I did not confirm a data table outside chat.
steps: Ask the chat for a table with three columns and three rows.
Compare the space around the text in each cell.
Check cells in every row use the same padding.
S6.16.where: Effect seen in tables in chat replies

S6.17.note: The turn spacing value is inner CSS.
steps: Send two messages in one chat.
Measure the gap between the first reply and the next user message.
Compare that gap with the gap between the next user message and its reply.
S6.17.where: Effect seen between two chat turns in one conversation

S6.18.note: Whether the toolbar always shows or only on hover at phone width was not verified.
steps: Send a message and wait for the reply.
Move the pointer over the reply, or tap it on a phone.
Look at the gap between the reply text and the toolbar below it.
Compare that gap with the spacing used by other replies.
S6.18.where: Chat reply > hover the reply (action toolbar with Copy message, Good response, Bad response, Regenerate response)

S6.19.note: Composer padding is an inner CSS rule; I did not confirm exact visible label text for the composer.
steps: Click New chat.
Look at the space between the box edge and the text, and between the box edge and its buttons.
Type a long line and compare the padding with the empty box.
S6.19.where: Effect seen in the message box at the bottom of a new chat

S6.20.note: Gutter values are inner CSS; the check is the visible margin.
steps: Open Settings, then Appearance.
Resize the browser window to a wide width and note the left and right margin.
Narrow the window to phone width and check the margin gets smaller in steps, not jumps.
S6.20.where: Effect seen at the left and right edges of chat and Settings pages when the window width changes

S6.21.needs: a few conversations in the account
S6.21.note: The row height is inner CSS; I did not verify the exact row height.
steps: Open the sidebar with several conversations listed.
Measure the height of each row.
Compare the rows: each should be the same height.
S6.21.where: Effect seen in the sidebar conversation list

S6.22.note: I did not identify the second menu to compare; only the Account menu was checked.
steps: Click the Account menu button at the bottom of the sidebar.
Read the menu items, such as Settings.
Measure or compare the row height and padding of each item.
Open another dropdown menu in the app and compare item heights.
S6.22.where: Account menu > Settings (menu items are in the Account menu list)

S6.23.note: I did not locate a second dialog to compare against.
steps: Click the Account menu button, then Settings.
Measure the inner padding around the title and the content.
Open a confirmation or sheet dialog from another place in the app and compare its padding.
S6.23.where: Account menu > Settings (the Settings dialog) and any confirmation dialog

S6.24.note: The form-field spacing rule is inner CSS; the General section was the form I located.
steps: Click Account menu, then Settings, then General.
Measure the gap between a field label and its control.
Measure the gap between two fields.
Compare the gaps across rows.
S6.24.where: Settings > General (label-to-input spacing and field-to-field spacing)

S6.25.note: The icon grid and stroke are inner code values.
steps: Open the Account menu.
Compare the icon size and stroke weight of Settings with other menu icons.
Open the sidebar and compare its icons with the menu icons.
S6.25.where: Effect seen on icons in the sidebar and the Account menu

S6.26.note: Button sizes (default, xs, sm, lg, icon) are defined in packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Button.tsx and there is no in-app density setting. Nothing for the tester to switch.
S6.26.where: No control; button sizes are set in code and seen on any button

S6.27.note: Radius values come from the design tokens and Button.tsx; there is no setting for them.
steps: Open any menu or dialog in the app.
Compare the corner rounding of its panel and buttons with the page around it, then compare with Expected.
S6.27.where: No control; corner radii show on buttons, cards and menus

S6.28.note: Shadow scale is set in design tokens and primitives such as Dialog.tsx; no in-app control.
steps: Open any menu or dialog in the app.
Look at the edge and shadow of the raised panel against the page, then compare with Expected.
S6.28.where: No control; shadows show on open menus and dialogs

S6.29.note: The z-index ladder is in the design tokens and Dialog.tsx; a tester can only see its effect in stacking.
steps: Open a menu, then open a dialog from the app.
Check the dialog sits above the menu and the page, and that the menu does not show through, then compare with Expected.
S6.29.where: No control; stacking order shows when a dialog opens over other layers

S6.30.note: Durations are set in the design tokens and Sheet.tsx; there is no in-app setting for them.
steps: Open a menu or dialog, then close it.
Watch the timing and easing of the open and close, then compare with Expected.
S6.30.where: No control; durations and easing show when menus, dialogs and sheets open and close

S6.31.note: The in-app Reduced option sets a page attribute; the OS reduce-motion setting is changed outside the app and the 'System' choice follows it. The 'Settings' menu entry was not confirmed in the account footer file.
steps: Open Settings from the account menu and choose Appearance.
Under Motion, click Reduced.
Open a chat and send a message, then watch the reply and any loading animation.
Compare what moves with Expected: looping or travelling animation should stop or become gentle. Set Motion back to System afterwards.

S6.32.note: Code blocks also have their own 'Code theme' setting in the same section, so the tester should check code blocks against that setting as well.
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Under Theme, click Light and look at the whole page, including a code block in a reply.
Click Dark and look again, then click System.
Compare with Expected: each choice should change the whole surface, including code.
S6.32.where: Settings > Appearance > Theme > Light, Dark or System

S6.33.note: System follows the device's own contrast setting, which lives outside the app and was not tested from the code.
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Set Contrast to High.
Look at text, borders and dividers on the chat page and in a menu.
Press Tab to move focus across buttons and compare the focus ring with Expected. Set Contrast back to System afterwards.

S6.34.note: States are styled in packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/Button.tsx; there is no separate control for them.
steps: Open Settings and choose Appearance.
Move the pointer over a Theme button, then press Tab to focus one.
Click and hold a button to see its pressed look, then compare the states with Expected.
S6.34.where: No control; hover, focus, press and disabled looks show on any button

S6.35.note: Icons are set in apps/web/app/manifest.ts and the sidebar wordmark in apps/web/shared/components/agi/SidebarWordmark.tsx; the visible wording of the wordmark was not read.
steps: After signing in, look at the top of the sidebar for the brand mark.
Compare the mark and the app icon with Expected.
S6.35.where: Sidebar top row (brand mark) and the browser tab or installed app icon
